titel: One place decides which state means done
warum: A message has four states. Every reader interpreted for itself which of them are through, and no two agreed. Measured once: a delivery check compared against a state that does not exist and therefore reported every message as open; another reported 123 open where 83 were open. None of them was mistyped - all were correct back when there were two states.
pruefung: No module outside the inbox module compares against a closing state. Setting one is fine, interpreting one is not.

titel: The agent-name rule exists once
warum: A message filename embeds an agent name twice. A second, stricter copy of the rule inside the name parser rejected every name carrying a hyphen or a digit - mail for 'vm-admin' counted as unreadable and was never announced. A silent allowlist nobody had decided on.
pruefung: The parser composes its pattern from the shared name fragment instead of retyping one. A test reads a name with a hyphen.

titel: Two clones never form the same message name
warum: Same sender, same recipient, same second yields the same filename with different content. Both clones are allowed to - each creates exclusively and cannot see the other. In git that is an add/add conflict; a watcher that commits the conflict markers makes the whole drawer unreadable and delivery silent. Once for eight hours.
pruefung: The name carries a mark rolled once per clone. Two fresh clones write the same message and get different names.

titel: A disambiguated name stays readable
warum: The collision counter hung as '-2' directly off the recipient name. An agent name may contain hyphens, so it could not be told apart - the parser returned null, and a name that does not parse counts as unreadable and is never announced as new. The repair against data loss had produced an undeliverable message.
pruefung: The second message of the same second is written AND read back, and the recipient is right.

titel: A clone's runtime state never leaves it
warum: The state directory describes exactly one container. A number carried from there to another machine is invented. And since the clone mark lives there, a travelling directory would move the add/add conflict from the messages onto the mark - the same outage under a new name.
pruefung: The state directory is in .gitignore. Deliberately shared single files sit next to it as named exceptions.

titel: No decision depends on a field nothing writes
warum: Four times in ten days: a guard reads a field, no write path sets it, the guard silently does nothing. A guard that never fires looks exactly like one with nothing to report - each time that cost weeks instead of minutes.
pruefung: An instrument intersects the fields a decision depends on with the fields the corpus knows, and reports the empty ones.

titel: A measurement run does not inherit the measuring machine's start context
warum: A measurement run invoked the agent tool as a subprocess. That runs the session-start hooks - for a benchmark exactly as for a session. Nine of 192 answers came out of the operator's own memory instead of the test corpus; their hallucination count was worthless, because the model had read those numbers rather than invented them.
pruefung: Every measuring call passes the flag that keeps foreign hooks out, with the reason written beside it. A positive control fails if the probe stops finding the harnesses.

titel: An instrument that checked nothing does not pass
warum: The whole family of defects these instruments chase is 'a check that silently does nothing'. An instrument reporting 'no finding' on an empty corpus, or on patterns that no longer match, is one of them.
pruefung: Nothing checked yields its own exit value, not zero. Every instrument carries a positive control against the real corpus.

titel: Not measured is not the same as zero
warum: A channel without a measuring point needs a measuring point; a channel with zero consumption needs a repair. Reporting both as 0 builds the wrong thing.
pruefung: Reports carry 'not measured' as its own value. A test fails if it turns into a 0.

titel: Alias table for spelling variants - measured, not built
zahl: Field tags: 845 values, 56 % used exactly once, but only 24 resp. 20 spelling variants under two independent normalisations (3 % / 2 %). Field class: 185 values, 74 % once, 1 resp. 0 variants.
warum: The dispersion sits in the vocabulary, not in the spelling. Nobody types the same word differently - everyone picks a different word. The single-use values are not typos but different terms. An alias table would have collected 2.5 % and created maintenance. That also answers 'who maintains the aliases': nobody.
neu_pruefen_wenn: The share of spelling variants rises above 15 %. A test fails then.

titel: Cut 'field read in code, never written in code'
zahl: 222 candidates, nearly all file extensions and standard library.
warum: Too wide. Most fields a program reads are not corpus fields.
neu_pruefen_wenn: Not - the narrower cut (a decision depends on it AND the corpus knows it) is built and holds.

titel: Cut 'field read in code, absent from the corpus'
zahl: 714 of 727 - unusable for the same reason.
warum: A field the corpus has never seen is almost always a local variable and none of our business. Mixed in with the real findings it buries eleven answers under seven hundred.
neu_pruefen_wenn: Not. 'Unknown' is reported separately and is explicitly not a finding.

titel: Using the agent tool's hook-free flag for measurement runs
zahl: Positive control before 192 calls: the flag disables the hooks and breaks authentication doing so (it wants an API key). A settings flag with empty hooks did not help either - the user-level file is merged in regardless.
warum: Found by measuring, not by reading the help text. Only the restricting flag passed the control.
neu_pruefen_wenn: The agent tool changes its flags. The positive control is the question answerable ONLY from the hook text.

titel: What counts as a closing row is decided in one place per reader
warum: A record is closed append-only: a new row points at the original. Where two names exist for that pointer, every reader must know both. The memory core had learned this in an earlier round; a freshly built funnel read only the first name and reported 33 instead of 35 closed duties. And the same trap twice inside one function: the originals filter reads the same pointer, so a closing row counted as a NEW open duty - 68 produced instead of 66. Produced rises, consumed stands still, and that reads as a channel going bad. The same lesson from the MEASURING side, the same day: counting over an append-only book means naming the folding rule before counting. The measuring point 'last entry per id' yielded 20 waiting proposals; a request is decided by a LATER row naming it through a concerns-pointer, so no decision row hid its request and all 20 stayed on 'waiting'. Folded, ONE was open. Without the folding rule you count rows and mean records.
pruefung: One helper per reader decides what a closing row is, and both places ask it. A test writes one row per pointer name and checks produced AND consumed. And every count over an append-only book names its folding rule where the counting happens.

titel: A peer the test suite needs is installed by a plain install, not by hand
warum: An optional peer dependency is the right declaration for a feature the product works without. But no package manager installs an optional peer by itself. A suite whose tests load one is then green exactly on the machines where somebody once installed it by hand, and red everywhere else. Measured: CI failed on every one of 153 runs, on every platform, for days, while the same suite was green on a developer machine. The difference was invisible because the tests discarded the subprocess stderr and reported a null dereference instead of the message the program printed.
pruefung: Every optional peer that a test actually loads is also a devDependency AND carries a lockfile entry - devDependencies without a lockfile entry is a promise a clean install does not keep. A counter-check keeps the peer optional for users, so fixing the suite cannot quietly make the feature mandatory.

titel: A subprocess that stays silent must say why
warum: A test spawns a program, asserts on its output, and drops the exit status, the signal, the spawn error and stderr. When it fails, the whole message is 'nothing came back' - not the code, and not the lines the program itself printed. Found three times in one day. Measured once: 153 CI runs red, on every platform, while the same suite was green elsewhere; the cause had been sitting in the discarded stderr the whole time. Five days, three test files. Repairing the blindfold came BEFORE the fix and is what revealed the cause on the next run.
pruefung: A helper that spawns a subprocess carries exit status, signal, spawn error and stderr, and turns them into the assertion message. Where silence is a legitimate answer it must not throw, but must still carry the cause. A bolt reports new files with the same blindfold; a named legacy list may shrink and never grow.

titel: A path handed in from outside is normalised before it is used as a path
warum: On Windows an agent hands a shell hook a native path with backslashes. A test like [ -f "$k/.mem/config.json" ] then finds nothing, and the hook exits 0 without a word - indistinguishable from 'nothing to report'. Every hook in one of the houses was inert on Windows for as long as it had existed, the retrieval hook included, and nothing said so. Found only because a test comment recorded the promise that a real user runs Windows. Reproduced WITHOUT Windows: the same memory answers with 440 characters addressed with slashes and with nothing addressed with backslashes, exit 0 both times.
pruefung: Every hook that resolves a root itself substitutes backslashes for slashes before the lookup. Two guards: one that names any hook missing the substitution, and a counter-check that the helper really substitutes - a helper that is present and wrong would satisfy a guard that only looks for its name. Where a house documents that it never runs on Windows, a test holds that scope decision instead, and fails when it changes.

titel: A pattern that reads a real path accepts either separator
warum: Three separate places in one hook wrote a forward slash into code that handles a path: the root lookup, dirname of $0, and the pattern selecting which lanes warn. On Windows each of them matched nothing, and each made the hook exit 0 in silence. Two of the three were found by repairing a plausible cause and were real bugs, and NEITHER was the reported failure - the third one was. Only a trace naming each early exit ended the guessing, in one run.
pruefung: Patterns matching a path segment use a separator class, not a literal slash, with a positive control that the pattern is still present at all. Every early exit in a hook names itself behind a switch, so a failure says WHICH branch it took instead of only that nothing came back.

titel: Whoever counts over an append-only book prints the fold rule next to the number
warum: In an append-only book a request row keeps its own state field forever; it is decided by a LATER row that names it through a pointer. Group by id and every decision row forms its own group, hiding nobody - so all requests stay on 'waiting', which is the UNFOLDED count. Measured in the sibling project this tool was extracted from: 39 rows, reported to its owner as twenty waiting requests, folded it was ONE, and the report cost him the request to set states that had been set for nine days. The session counted correctly and named the right file; the reading instruction was written nowhere, and grouping by id is the reading a newcomer arrives at on their own. The same shape has struck twice inside this one instrument, when a reader copied one of two closing-pointer names.
pruefung: Every channel of a consumption measurement carries a required fold field and prints it next to the number - including the early returns for 'not measured', because that is where a required field is forgotten. Explicitly unfolded is a value of its own (NO_FOLD) and not the empty string: three states, never two. Plus a positive control that the printed sentence names the pointer actually folded on - a rule narrowed to one of two names would otherwise keep looking right while the number went wrong.

titel: A switch that narrowly misses a reserved name is a typo, not a field
warum: The log commands take any --name value as a field, which is what lets one store fit a domain it has never met. The cost showed on 2026-09-17, produced by hand: --projekt instead of --project. No message. The near miss became a FIELD on the entry, and because no project had been named the entry was filed globally instead of in the project. One keystroke, two wrong outcomes, exit 0. Found only because the success line prints the path and somebody read it. The open vocabulary is not the bug - the silence is.
zahl: Measured over the 235 distinct --switch names one house really uses: 'project' (7 chars) at distance <=2 catches 0 of them, at <=3 it catches 2; 'root' (4 chars) at <=1 catches 0, at <=2 it catches 6 (font, host, out, port, role, tool). So one flat number is wrong in both directions, and the tolerance has to depend on length.
pruefung: The reserved names and the near-miss rule live in ONE module, and the probe imports that module instead of recomputing the rule - a probe with its own copy stays green when the rule moves. The probe re-measures the thresholds against the repo's real switch corpus, refuses a corpus that has collapsed, and drives the real CLI end to end: the typo is refused AND nothing is written, while an ordinary field still becomes a field.

titel: The same calculation is implemented once
warum: Three narrower invariants already say it for one vocabulary each (closing state, agent name, closing pointer). The general form was carried in test markers for days without a catalogue entry - and on 2026-09-18 it bit in the sibling house, in one repo, on one day: src/roh.mjs states that a capture's SIZE comes from the ledger and not from disk, and reasons about it at length. bin/mem-fasser.sh, a few hundred lines away, called statSync itself. Four captures that had moved to the archive came back ENOENT, counted as infinitely large, and were pushed to the back of the queue where they could only be processed one at a time. The comment was right, well written, and guarded by nothing.
pruefung: For a question the house answers by calculation - a size, a dueness, an open count - exactly one exported function computes it, and every other call site imports that one. A second implementation of the same arithmetic is the defect, even when both are correct today.

titel: A view never falls back to invented data
warum: A viewer whose fetch fails and which then renders plausible sample rows is worse than one that renders nothing: the page is convincing, and the status strip still claims 'live'. Nobody checks a page that looks right. The marker for this rule sat in the sibling house's desk module and its test for days with no catalogue entry, so the other house never learned it - and it has a viewer too.
pruefung: No rendering path substitutes example, demo or placeholder rows when the real read fails. Three states: data / no data, said so / could not read, said so.

titel: Not measurable is not zero
warum: A gauge that reports 'could not measure' as 0 reports health where nothing was checked, and it does so in the quietest possible way: a zero looks like a clean result. The same shape appeared twice in one day in the sibling house - a capture of unknown size counted as free, and a doctor finding that read 'inactive' as 'broken' for a unit that is inactive between runs by design.
pruefung: Every gauge distinguishes a measured zero from an unmeasurable value, and renders the second as its own state - never folded into the first.

titel: Linting comments for normative wording - measured, not built
zahl: Measured in the sister house, whose comment style this one shares: 636 comment lines in src/ and bin/ contain must/never/always/may not (in German); 2213 contain a four-plus-letter all-caps word used for emphasis, the commonest being NICHT (156), JSON (64), JSONL (28), HTTP (22), HEAD (21) - mostly acronyms and identifiers, not rules.
warum: The proposal: a comment that STATES a rule rather than explaining one must name a test or an id. The occasion was real - on 2026-09-18 two defects each had a well-written rule comment and nothing checking it. But the house style is precisely to argue rules in prose, so every good piece of reasoning would be a hit. At that hit rate the lint gets switched off within days, and then it stops catching the guilty too. What was built instead is the explicit marker (bench/calculations.mjs in this house): mechanically checkable, no false positives.
neu_pruefen_wenn: A phrase turns up that occurs ONLY in rule comments - then the detection problem is solved and only the whitelist remains. Or: a third defect appears in a file that owns no catalogued calculation, where the marker cannot reach it.
